updates.rationale: Independent pursuit requires framing the multiletter achievability program, reconciling normalization and benchmarks, surveying applicable Marton reductions, and coordinating its proof and computational routes. It is a plausible but specialized branch of the exact-capacity effort.

A separate agenda-setting pass would formulate candidate multiletter constructions, identify support-size questions, and prioritize analytic versus computational investigations before the key restriction is independently known.

Once the program is pursued, support pruning is a natural high-incidence bottleneck. Without access, the community must independently discover the relevant support-cardinality restriction, prove that the binary-alphabet reduction applies to induced subchannels, check the product benchmark comparison, and build rigorous computational or symbolic validation.

Before independent discovery of a pruning theorem, researchers are likely to spend substantial effort exploring parametrizations, support patterns, symmetry reductions, numerical optimizations, and failed low-support constructions. This broad search remains a common parallel route within the program.
